# gsuite_known_failures / pptx

Fixtures for failure modes discovered by the Google Workspace
roundtrip oracle (Spec 031). Each known-failure has both a
**bad** form (triggers the failure) and a **good** form (with the
specific construct fixed) so regression tests can cover both ends
of the bisection.

## bee-with-stroke-zero.pptx (bad) / bee-without-stroke-zero.pptx (good)

**Failure mode:** Google Slides' `files.copy` import returns
`HTTP 500 Internal Error` when an OOXML package contains
`<a:path stroke="0">` inside a `<a:custGeom>`.

**Origin:** Generated by [`svg2ooxml`](../../../../../svg2ooxml/) from
`../../../../../svg2ooxml/assets/bee-flying-svg.svg` — a 250×250
flying-bee SVG converted to a single-slide PPTX with 33 custom-geom
shapes.

**Why it breaks:** The shape's outline is already suppressed at the
shape level via `<p:spPr><a:ln><a:noFill/></a:ln></p:spPr>`. The
path-level `stroke="0"` is redundant. PowerPoint, LibreOffice, and
Word all accept the redundancy silently. Google Slides' import
engine returns a hard 500 — not even a useful error message,
just `{"reason": "internalError"}`.

**Bisection evidence (May 2026):** Reduced bee.pptx to a single
shape kept failing with HTTP 500. Stripping `<p:timing>`: still
fails. Replacing `<a:custGeom>` with `<a:prstGeom prst="rect"/>`:
imports cleanly. Keeping the exact original `<a:custGeom>` path
points but removing only the `stroke="0"` attribute on `<a:path>`:
imports cleanly. Single-attribute root cause.

**Fix in svg2ooxml:** `src/svg2ooxml/drawingml/generator.py` — drop
the `stroke="0"` emission when stroke_mode is `"false"`/`"0"`/`"none"`.
Outline suppression at the shape level is sufficient and
cross-renderer compatible.

**Regression test:**
`tests/test_gsuite_oracle_known_failures.py::test_stroke_zero_breaks_gsuite_import`
— skipped without GSuite creds; documents the failure even when
not running live.

## File layout

```
bee-with-stroke-zero.pptx       # 15.9 KB — 33 paths with stroke="0"
bee-without-stroke-zero.pptx    # 15.9 KB — same shapes, attribute removed
```

The two files differ only in the 33 `stroke="0"` attributes;
slide geometry and structure are otherwise identical.
